text:
Ben: Customer X is seeing intermittent 504s from the hosted API edge after they switch tenants. Happening ~1-2% of requests, mostly streaming/chat calls. Started ~10m after a tenant config change.
Ellen: Do you have trace IDs or sample request/response for a 504?
Ben: Yep, seeing trace ids: trace=tr-8b3f, tr-8b7a. Attached curl repro below.
Ben: ```curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'X-Tenant-ID: tenant-42' 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream' --data '{"messages": [{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'```
Alice: Noticed pattern: spike right after tenant switch when requests are mid-flight, connection stays open then gateway returns 504. Could be upstream pool exhaustion or h2 stream limit. :thinking_face: 
Ingrid: Any deploys/rollouts around that time? I see a private control-plane change pushed 11m ago.
deploy-bot: deploy/redwood-control-plane v2.14.1 -> v2.14.2 deployed by ingrid at 2026-03-17T10:12:34Z (10m ago). Health checks OK.
Ben: Customer says it began ~2-3 minutes after the change, so timeline matches.
Ellen: Can you paste an envoy/nginx edge log snippet with the trace id? We need upstream response code and stream error.
Ben: ```[2026-03-17T10:15:01Z] trace=tr-8b3f method=POST path=/v1/chat/stream status=504 upstr_resp=RESET reason="upstream connection reset" src=10.8.1.22:443```
Alice: Also seeing `RST_STREAM 2` in tcp logs for that client connection, but upstream internal pool still shows available sockets.
Ellen: Two hypotheses: 1) auth/billing proxy added a short-circuit that returns 504 on tenant header mismatch during in-flight token swap; 2) mux retry loop on midstream tenant routing causing envoy to cancel stream then fallback.
Ingrid: We rolled a small change to tenant routing sticky map — it updated backends for tenant-42. Could cause connection pinning mismatch for active h2 streams.
Ben: Customer repro steps: 1) Start long streaming chat, 2) Trigger tenant switch via admin API, 3) ~2-3m later stream ends with 504.
Ellen: Good repro. Can we reproduce internally? Alice, can you run the same with a local frontend proxy to emulate sticky map update?
Alice: Running now, will post quick logs.
Alice: ```CLIENT: stream open -> server sends partial tokens -> admin changes tenant backend -> server stops sending -> client sees 504 from edge after ~120s idle```
Ellen: That 120s idle smells like an upstream idle timeout kicking in after connection is no longer pinned. Check keepalive and idle_window settings on edge.
Ingrid: Current edge config has idle_timeout=120s for h2 streams and connection_pool rehash on routing changes enabled. We can try a quick patch to extend idle_timeout to 300s for tenant updates during rollout window.
Ben: Customer is hitting production now, can we provide a mitigation first? Maybe instruct customer to retry with smaller streaming chunks or temporary non-stick routing?
Ellen: Immediate mitigation: configure fallback routing so in-flight streams are drained rather than rehashed. I'll open a short-lived canary to disable rehash for 20m.
Ingrid: I'll push a rollback-safe toggle: `edge.routing.rehash_on_update=false` for canary cluster, 2mins to roll.
deploy-bot: canary toggle applied to cluster edge-canary-3 by Ingrid at 2026-03-17T10:23:05Z.
Ben: Reporting back to customer with canary and suggested retry pattern.
Alice: Repro locally looks stable with toggle off, no immediate 504s after tenant switch.
Ellen: Next actions: 1) Monitor canary for 30m, 2) collect more envoy traces for affected traces, 3) consider increasing idle_timeout for tenant update window. I'll create a follow-up ticket for config change if canary is stable.
Ben: Thanks — I'll update customer and paste follow-up ticket id once created. :thumbsup:
